Evelyn / Kimberly,

Attaching BlueHorizon’s completed order form and the MSA draft they returned after our call yesterday. Key asks from the customer: 1) shorten SLA response windows where possible, 2) confirm multi-region residency options (US + EU), and 3) clarify billing cadence for usage overages.

We need a quick pass from legal on major no-gos and a proposed redline window. They want to close in ~3 weeks, but we should be realistic — I expect several rounds. Can you call out priority clauses (indemnity, data residency, IP, export controls) and suggest a signature pathway (who signs — customer PO vs exec sign)?

Attachments: BlueHorizon_MSA_v1.1.docx (MSA), BH_OrderForm_Draft.xlsx (Order Form)

Thanks,
Jordan

Thanks Jordan — looping in our legal team (contracts@bluehorizon.ai). We attached our annotated PDF with redlines and a short comment doc listing three negotiation priorities:

- Service levels: we propose a targeted P1 response of 1 hour and a 99.6% monthly uptime on the dedicated tier.
- Data residency: primary region US-W (Oregon), with optional failover in EU-W; need written confirmation of geo-fencing processes.
- Liability cap: BH requests a liability cap equal to the amount paid in the prior 12 months.

We’ve attached BlueHorizon_Redlines_v1.pdf that shows our edits on the MSA and a separate sheet with Order Form line-item clarifications. If you can send your redline key (clause-level comments + acceptance matrix) that would help speed the counter.

Sophie Lang
Head of Ops, BlueHorizon Analytics

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — initial package for legal review

Thanks Jordan — Sophie, appreciate the annotated PDF. I did a first-pass read and called out a few items below. Kimberly, can you take ownership of the counter-draft? I’ve dropped targeted notes into the canary redlines sheet and highlighted the clause heatmap.

High-level assessment (first pass):
- Data residency / geo-fencing: acceptable to document optional EU failover but we need explicit operational controls (KMS key residency, egress logging). Recommend counter language that allows failover with contractually required notice and audit access.
- SLAs: we can tighten response windows for priority incidents but won’t commit to a 1-hour P1 on dedicated unless tied to a higher tier. Propose: P1 response acknowledgement within 1 hour, remediation SLA layered by tier.
- Liability cap: standard Redwood stance is a capped liability tied to fees in the prior 12 months for most deals, but we can offer a step-up for strategic/enterprise accounts. Ask: Jordan — can you confirm expected ARR if this helps pricing/limit trade-off?
- IP & export controls: their edits on IP assignment are aggressive — Kimberly, please flag specific redline lines 4.2–4.5 for escalation.

Next steps / asks:
1) Kimberly to provide counterredline (MSA) by COB Monday (2027-12-07) with: clause change summary, risk tier (low/medium/high), and suggested concession path.
2) Jordan to share anticipated ARR/contract value for deal economics (helps negotiation of liability cap).
3) Sophie / BH to confirm procurement steps (PO only vs signed MSA) and whether security questionnaires or SOC 2 report will be required in the buyer’s procurement portal.
4) I'll prepare a short decision tree for signatures (PO -> standard SOW; Exec sign -> if > $X ARR or data residency exceptions) and share the Draft DocuSign template link for their legal to review.

Attachments referenced: BlueHorizon_Redlines_v1.pdf, canary redlines sheet: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-canary-redlines, DocuSign template preview: https://app.docusign.com/templates/templ_5238

Kimberly — please confirm you can take the counter and call out any clauses that require Legal Director escalation. I’ll queue an internal triage meeting if more than three high-risk clauses appear.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwood.com
